results.content:
This is part of a larger report on the attitudes and dynamics shaping the 2026 midterm elections.

With several weeks to go until Election Day, Americans who are registered to vote favor Democrats over Republicans in the national race for the House of Representatives by an 8 percentage point margin (44% to 36%). About two-in-ten registered voters say they would vote for a third-party candidate or are not sure.

Midterm vote preferences in key demographic groups [...] Voters ages 18 to 29 prefer Democrats over Republicans by a two-to-one margin: 51% to 23%. A quarter say they are not sure or would support another candidate.
 Voters 30 to 49 tilt toward Democrats – 43% vs. 31% for Republicans

In Decision Desk HQ’s generic ballot average, the Democrats' lead has increased to about 8 points, 49%-41%. This measurement of the national electoral environment has boosted Democrats’ position as clearer favorites in DDHQ’s House forecast and as very slight favorites in our Senate forecast. Democrats have led in Decision Desk HQ’s generic ballot average since last year, and at least 6 points since early August.

The map favors Republicans, but cracks in their base are leaving them vulnerable in defending House and Senate control.
